content.text:
Re-submitted with the intent defect repaired.

**What changed from the prior version:** Operation 1 on Section 11.1 now covers both the fee amount and the immediately following applicability sentence. That sentence previously excluded "an Event of Default on the part of Customer or M&I", which contradicted amended 11.2(A) (where the same fee is imposed precisely on a Customer Event of Default). It now reads "...other than pursuant to an Event of Default on the part of M&I or pursuant to Section 11.3 below, and shall also apply as provided in Section 11.2(A)", so 11.1 and 11.2(A) are consistent and no "notwithstanding" override is needed.

**Unchanged and verified:**
- Operation 2 (11.2(A)) folds the duplicate cause fee into the single Termination for Convenience Fee; the trailing sentence referring to the now-undefined "Termination for Cause Fee" is deleted as a consequence, and the unfavourable 13.4 carve-out for the Convenience Fee in 11.1 is left intact.
- Operation 3 (13.5) confirms the fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by us and that no other Customer payment is liquidated damages or a penalty.
- Notice periods, instalment timing and all other commercial language remain verbatim; minimality and anchors validated ok:true.

The rationale also flags for the client, as a commercial (non-element) point, that the three-month fee remains payable on any Customer Event of Default however minor, so a materiality/cure qualifier would fully close the minor-breach walk-away concern.
